questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.learningObjective: Count rows preserved by a left join
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins 10 customers to orders with a left join. Three customers have no orders. How many customer rows survive?

options.text: Ten, because left join keeps all left rows
Seven, because unmatched customers drop out
options.misconception: confuses left join with inner join

options.text: Zero, because NULLs are filtered out

questions.explanation: A left join preserves every row from the left table. Unmatched customers appear with NULL order columns.
questions.hint: Left side rows are always kept.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins users to roles where one user has 3 roles. How many rows does that user produce?

options.text: One row, because users are unique
Three rows, one per matching role
Zero rows, because duplicates are removed

questions.explanation: A join produces one row per matching pair. One user with three roles yields three rows.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.learningObjective: Explain sum inflation from duplicate joins
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins orders to line items and sums order totals. Why might the sum be too high?

answer.exemplar: If one order has multiple line items, the order total is repeated per line item, so summing line-item rows inflates the order total.

questions.explanation: Joining at a finer grain repeats parent values. Aggregating without adjusting for grain inflates sums.
questions.hint: Parent values repeat per child row.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.learningObjective: Count rows removed by a filter
questions.stem: A dashboard note starts with 50 events and filters WHERE status = 'active', leaving 32. How many rows did the filter remove?
questions.explanation: Subtract the remaining rows from the original count: 50 minus 32 equals 18 removed rows.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.stem: A dashboard note compares each sale to its region average. Which SQL pattern finds rows above their group average?

options.text: WHERE amount > AVG(amount) GROUP BY region
WHERE amount > AVG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY region)

options.misconception: returns only top row not group comparison

questions.explanation: A window average computes the group mean per row, allowing a WHERE comparison. GROUP BY aggregates cannot be used directly in WHERE.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.stem: A dashboard note has 40 orders and a correlated subquery in SELECT. How many evaluations occur?

options.text: One, because SELECT subqueries are cached
Zero, because SELECT does not execute subqueries

questions.explanation: Correlated subqueries run once per outer row. Forty orders mean forty evaluations.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.stem: A dashboard note computes SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date) for 5 rows with amounts 2,3,4,5,6. What is the value on the last row?
questions.explanation: The running total accumulates all rows through the current row, so the last row holds the grand total 20.
questions.hint: Last row holds the grand total.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.stem: A dashboard note ranks sales 10,10,12,14 with DENSE_RANK. What rank does 12 receive?

answer.exemplar: DENSE_RANK gives 12 a rank of 2 because the two 10s share rank 1 and the next distinct value gets the next integer with no gap.

questions.explanation: Dense rank assigns the same rank to ties and the next integer to the next distinct value, with no gaps.

questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.learningObjective: Contrast left and inner join counts
questions.stem: A dashboard note left joins 8 customers to orders and gets 12 rows. An inner join on the same tables gets 9 rows. How many customer rows had no orders?
questions.explanation: The difference between left and inner join rows is the unmatched left rows: 12 minus 9 equals 3 customers without orders.
questions.hint: Subtract inner count from left count.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins 2 students to 3 courses where each student takes 2 courses and one course is shared. How many rows result?
questions.explanation: Each student-course pair produces a row. Two students times two courses each equals four rows, with the shared course counted twice.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.stem: A dashboard note duplicates each order 3 times via a join. If the true total is 100, what sum appears?

options.text: 300, because each value is counted three times

questions.explanation: Triplicating each row triples the sum. 100 times 3 equals 300.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.stem: A dashboard note filters rows with WHERE before grouping. What did the filter remove?

options.text: Whole groups that fail the predicate
Individual rows that fail the predicate
Nothing, because WHERE runs after grouping

questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping. HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.stem: A dashboard note has region sales 10,20,30. How many sales are above their region average?

answer.exemplar: The region average is 20, so only the sale of 30 is above the average, giving one row.

questions.explanation: The average of 10, 20, and 30 is 20. Comparing each value to 20 leaves one row above.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.stem: A dashboard note has 25 rows. An uncorrelated subquery evaluates once. How many fewer evaluations than a correlated version?
questions.explanation: Correlated evaluates 25 times; uncorrelated evaluates once. The difference is 24 fewer evaluations.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.stem: A dashboard note uses SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING). What is the last row's value?

options.text: The cumulative sum through the last row

questions.explanation: UNBOUNDED PRECEDING accumulates from the first row through the current, so the last row holds the total.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.stem: A dashboard note ranks 4,4,6,8. How does DENSE_RANK differ from RANK for the value 6?

options.misconception: ignores the dense rank no-gap rule

questions.explanation: RANK leaves a gap after ties so 6 is rank 3. DENSE_RANK has no gap so 6 is rank 2.

questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.learningObjective: Explain NULL fill in left join
questions.stem: A dashboard note left joins customers to orders. A customer with no orders shows what in order columns?

options.misconception: confuses left join with inner join

questions.explanation: Unmatched left rows are preserved with NULL in right-table columns. No implicit zero or empty string is used.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.stem: A dashboard note shows inflated revenue after joining orders to items. What is the likely cause?

answer.exemplar: Joining orders to items multiplies order revenue by item count, so aggregating without deduplication or correct grain inflates revenue.

questions.explanation: Revenue stored at order grain repeats per item. Summing item rows counts each order multiple times.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.stem: A dashboard note has 4 orders totaling 200. A join duplicates each order twice. What sum appears?
questions.explanation: Each order is counted twice, so the sum doubles: 200 times 2 equals 400.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.stem: A dashboard note filters out cancelled orders before computing total revenue. What changed?

options.text: Cancelled orders no longer contribute to revenue

options.misconception: assumes filtering does not affect averages

questions.explanation: Filtering before aggregation removes cancelled rows, so they no longer affect sums or averages.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.stem: A dashboard note has region sales 5,10,15,20. How many are above the region average?
questions.explanation: The average is 12.5, so 15 and 20 are above it, giving two rows.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.stem: A dashboard note uses EXISTS with a correlated subquery over 60 rows. How many evaluations occur?

options.text: One hundred twenty, two per row

questions.explanation: EXISTS evaluates the correlated subquery per outer row, with early exit on first match.
questions.hint: Per outer row with early exit.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.stem: A dashboard note computes a running total of 3,4,5. What is the value after the second row?

answer.exemplar: The running total after the second row is 7 because 3 plus 4 equals 7.

questions.explanation: Cumulative sum adds each row to the previous total: 3 then 7 then 12.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.learningObjective: Compute dense rank for multiple ties
questions.stem: A dashboard note ranks 7,7,7,9 with DENSE_RANK. What rank does 9 receive?
questions.explanation: The three 7s share rank 1 and the next distinct value 9 gets rank 2 with no gap.

questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.stem: A dashboard note wants all customers even those without orders. Which join should be used?

options.text: RIGHT JOIN from orders to customers
INNER JOIN from customers to orders
LEFT JOIN from customers to orders
CROSS JOIN of customers and orders

questions.explanation: A left join preserves all customers while attaching matching orders. Inner join would drop customers without orders.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins two tables on a shared key where the key appears 4 times in each table. How many rows result?

options.text: Sixteen, the product of the counts

questions.explanation: A many-to-many join on a shared key produces the product of matching counts: 4 times 4 equals 16.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.stem: A dashboard note sum of order totals is 3x the known revenue. What is the likely cause?

options.text: The data has three times as many orders
A join duplicated each order three times

questions.explanation: A 3x inflation matches a join that triplicates each order. Correcting join grain fixes the sum.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.stem: A dashboard note applies a date filter in WHERE before SUM. Why does the total drop?

answer.exemplar: The filter removes rows outside the date range before aggregation, so their values no longer contribute to the sum.

questions.explanation: WHERE runs before GROUP BY and aggregates, excluding rows from all downstream calculations.
questions.hint: Filtered rows never reach the sum.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.learningObjective: Identify window function for group comparison
questions.stem: A dashboard note has group values 4,8,12. How many are strictly above the group average?
questions.explanation: The average is 8, so only 12 is strictly above it, giving one row.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.stem: A dashboard note uses an uncorrelated subquery in WHERE. How many times does it evaluate?

options.text: Zero times, because it is cached
Once, because it does not reference outer rows

questions.explanation: Without an outer reference, the subquery is evaluated once and its result reused for all rows.
questions.hint: No outer reference means one evaluation.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish running total from grand total
questions.stem: A dashboard note computes SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date) on row 3 of 5. Is this the grand total?

options.text: Yes, because ORDER BY implies full partition
Yes, window sums always include all rows
No, it is only row 3's amount
No, it is the cumulative sum through row 3

questions.explanation: With ORDER BY and default frame, the sum accumulates through the current row only, not the whole partition.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.learningObjective: Compute dense rank on first tied value
questions.stem: A dashboard note ranks 5,5,7,9 with DENSE_RANK. What rank do the two 5s receive?

options.misconception: confuses dense rank with row number

options.text: 0, because dense rank is zero based

questions.explanation: Dense rank assigns rank 1 to the first distinct value, so both 5s receive rank 1.

questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.stem: A dashboard note uses RIGHT JOIN instead of LEFT JOIN. What changes about which table is preserved?

answer.exemplar: RIGHT JOIN preserves the right table instead of the left, so unmatched right rows appear with NULL left columns.

questions.explanation: The preserved side is the one named by the join direction. RIGHT JOIN keeps right-table rows.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins 2 departments to 6 employees where each department has 3 employees. How many rows result?
questions.explanation: Each department matches 3 employees, so 2 times 3 equals 6 joined rows.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.stem: A dashboard note wants correct order totals despite an item join. Which fix works?

options.text: Aggregate items first, then join to orders

questions.explanation: Pre-aggregating items to order grain before joining prevents order totals from repeating.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.stem: A dashboard note uses HAVING COUNT(*) > 2. What does it remove?

options.misconception: confuses group filter with row filter

options.text: Groups with two or fewer rows

questions.explanation: HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Groups with count 2 or less are removed.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.stem: A dashboard note compares each sale to its group average using a correlated subquery. How many evaluations occur for 30 sales?

options.text: One, because the subquery is uncorrelated

questions.explanation: A correlated subquery evaluates per outer row, so 30 sales mean 30 evaluations.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.stem: A dashboard note uses EXISTS with a correlated subquery. Why might it be faster than a full subquery?

answer.exemplar: EXISTS stops evaluating as soon as it finds the first matching row, so it can avoid scanning the entire inner result.

questions.explanation: Early exit reduces work when a match exists. It still runs per outer row but may scan less.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.learningObjective: Compute frame sum for last row
questions.stem: A dashboard note has frame amounts 1,2,3,4. What is the running total on the last row?
questions.explanation: The cumulative sum through the last row is 1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 equals 10.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.stem: A dashboard note ranks 2,2,2,5 with DENSE_RANK. What rank does 5 receive?

options.text: 3, because ties count as one plus two
4, because three ties occupy three ranks

questions.explanation: Dense rank gives the three 2s rank 1 and the next distinct value 5 rank 2 with no gap.

questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.stem: A dashboard note left joins 5 customers to orders where 2 customers have 2 orders each. How many rows result?

options.text: 7, five customers plus two extra orders

questions.explanation: Each customer is preserved; customers with multiple orders produce multiple rows. 5 plus 2 extra orders equals 7.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins tags to posts on tag_id with 10 tags and 10 posts sharing one tag. What is the risk?
questions.explanation: A shared key appearing 10 times in each table yields 10 times 10 equals 100 joined rows.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.stem: A dashboard note sum of customer spend is 5x expected. What join issue could cause this?

answer.exemplar: A join duplicated each customer's spend five times, so summing the joined rows inflates the total by a factor of five.

questions.explanation: Duplicating joins repeat parent metrics. The inflation factor indicates the duplication factor.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.stem: A dashboard note filters 80 events to 55 active events. How many were removed?
questions.explanation: 80 minus 55 equals 25 removed rows.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.stem: A dashboard note wants rows where amount exceeds the group mean. Which clause is valid?

options.text: WHERE amount > AVG(amount) GROUP BY grp
WHERE amount > AVG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY grp)

questions.explanation: A window average computes the group mean per row, enabling a direct comparison in WHERE.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.stem: A dashboard note has 15 products and a correlated subquery in SELECT. How many evaluations occur?

options.text: Zero, because SELECT does not run subqueries

questions.explanation: Correlated subqueries evaluate per outer row. Fifteen products mean fifteen evaluations.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.stem: A dashboard note computes running total for amounts 6 and 4. What is the value after the second row?
questions.explanation: The running total after two rows is 6 plus 4 equals 10.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.stem: A dashboard note ranks 3,3,4,5 with DENSE_RANK. Why does 4 get rank 2 not 3?

answer.exemplar: DENSE_RANK assigns the same rank to ties and the next distinct value the next integer, so the two 3s are rank 1 and 4 is rank 2.

questions.explanation: Dense rank does not leave gaps after ties, unlike RANK which would give 4 rank 3.

questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.stem: A dashboard note left joins 12 customers to orders and gets 12 rows. How many customers had no orders?
questions.explanation: If every customer appears exactly once, all 12 had at least one order. No unmatched customers remain.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.learningObjective: Count rows after shared key join
questions.stem: A dashboard note joins 3 sellers to 3 buyers on city where 2 sellers and 2 buyers share a city. How many rows result for that city?
questions.explanation: Two sellers and two buyers in the same city produce 2 times 2 equals 4 joined rows.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.stem: A dashboard note sums revenue after joining orders to shipments. Revenue is 2x expected. What is the cause?

options.text: Each order has 2 shipments, duplicating revenue

questions.explanation: Two shipments per order duplicate order revenue. Pre-aggregating shipments fixes the sum.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.stem: A dashboard note filters WHERE active = true and count drops from 100 to 70. What did the filter remove?
questions.explanation: The filter removed the 30 rows where active is not true, leaving 70 active rows.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.stem: A dashboard note has group values 2,4,6. How many values are above the group average?

answer.exemplar: The average is 4, so only the value 6 is above it, giving one row.

questions.explanation: The mean of 2, 4, and 6 is 4. Only 6 exceeds 4.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.stem: A dashboard note has 18 orders and a correlated subquery in WHERE. How many evaluations occur?
questions.explanation: Correlated subqueries evaluate per outer row, so 18 orders mean 18 evaluations.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.stem: A dashboard note uses SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY date). What happens at a new region?

options.text: The running total becomes the grand total
The running total continues from the previous region
The running total resets to the first amount of that region
The running total is set to zero
options.misconception: resets to zero instead of first row

questions.explanation: PARTITION BY creates separate windows, so the running total restarts at the first row of each region.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.learningObjective: Compute dense rank for distinct values
questions.stem: A dashboard note ranks 1,2,3,4 with DENSE_RANK. What is the highest rank?

options.text: 0, because dense rank starts at zero

questions.explanation: With distinct values, dense rank assigns 1,2,3,4. The highest rank is 4.

questions.topic: Rows a left join preserves
questions.stem: A dashboard note wants all rows from both tables even without matches. Which join should be used?
questions.explanation: FULL OUTER JOIN preserves unmatched rows from both tables, filling NULLs on the missing side.

questions.topic: Row multiplication from a shared join value
questions.stem: A dashboard note row count explodes after joining. What is the likely cause?

answer.exemplar: A shared join key appears multiple times in both tables, creating a many-to-many explosion of rows.

questions.explanation: When both sides have duplicates on the join key, the result multiplies. Reducing duplicates or changing grain fixes it.

questions.topic: How much a duplicating join inflates a sum
questions.stem: A dashboard note duplicates each row 4 times via a join. If the true sum is 50, what sum appears?
questions.explanation: The sum is multiplied by the duplication factor: 50 times 4 equals 200.

questions.topic: What an earlier filter removed
questions.stem: A dashboard note applies an early WHERE filter. Which statement is true?

options.text: Filtered rows are excluded from all later aggregates

questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping and aggregation, so excluded rows never contribute to later results.
